VT.03.additionalInfo: Jin [f] — Metal. Wü [E] - Five. Wü - Five. The character "metal" in the name of the points suggests their influence on the lungs. In the Yellow River Diagram, five represents the earth's phase. The number five in the name of the points signifies their ability to treat phlegm and indicates the presence of five points. Point Name Sha [B] — External viral diseases characterized by pain and papules on the skin.

VT.05.additionalInfo: It is not necessary to use all 23 points. Palpate the points and needle only where the tone is high. Lee Kuo Zheng suggests that the points can be needled superficially, Threading the points on the five lines. Point Name Fü [Mi] — Hollow organs. Chåo — Nest. Érshisän [Z+E] - Twenty-three. The character Fu in the name of the points suggests their ability to treat intestinal diseases. Fü [F] — Hollow organs. The character Chao implies the points' ability to address gynecological disorders. The number 23 in the name indicates that there are 23 points.

VT.04.additionalInfo: These points are important for treating stomach diseases, especially when the area is very sensitive. They can also address stomach disorders that affect the heart and cause palpitations. The points are effective in treating intestinal issues that arise from stomach problems. Point Name Wéi [A] - Stomach. Måo — Hair. Qi — Seven. The number 7 in the name of the points indicates that there are seven points. In the Yellow River Diagram, seven represent fire, suggesting that these points influence the heart. QT [E] — Seven.
